text:
alex_h: Ran a full nsys capture on the 8-GPU cluster to chase the weird tail-latency spikes. attaching trace: s3://perf-traces/run-1765123456.nsys
maria_g: nice — what flags? did you include NCCL and NVTX?
alex_h: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --output=run-1765123456.nsys --sample=none \nCaptured at 512 tokens, batch size 8, kv-cache enabled across devices.
cheng_li: quick scan in Nsight timeline — I see a repeating pattern: compute kernels on GPUs 0..3 start, then a long idle gap while all-reduce runs, then GPUs 4..7 run. Looks like pipeline skew between TP groups.
ravi_k: can you share the kernel selection logs? might be falling back to slower matmul kernels for odd sequence lengths.
alex_h: pasted small excerpt from runtime log:\n```\n[2026-06-04T12:23:01Z] kernel_selector: selected=gemm_fp16_tiled, fallback=gemm_fp16_generic, seq_len=512\n[2026-06-04T12:23:01Z] kv_cache: routing=sharded_across_gpus, prefix_cache_hit=0.72\n```\nmaria_g: prefix_cache_hit 0.72 seems fine but routing=sharded_across_gpus could cause cross-device KV fetches during decode which interacts poorly with NCCL all-reduce timing.
perf-bot: perf-regression INF-2418 created for decode tail latency > 99th on multi-gpu run
cheng_li: looking at the NCCL timeline (in perfetto exported view) — all-reduce ops are aligned with kernel tails on group 0, but group 1's compute starts before the all-reduce finishes on group 0 -> visible serialization.
alex_h: exact symptom: concurrent request throughput ok, but single-request 99.9th spikes when seq_len ~512 and batching heuristics pack unevenly (last microbatch smaller -> kernel pick changes).
ravi_k: sounds like two interacting issues: batching heuristic creates uneven microbatches; kernel selector picks a different kernel for the smaller microbatch which has longer setup/warmup cost -> misaligned finish times -> NCCL waits.
maria_g: possible mitigations to try in order: 1) force homogeneous microbatch sizes for decode path (pad to max in batch), 2) pin kernel selection to the tiled GEMM for decode (override), 3) change KV routing to local-prefetch rather than sharded for short prefixes.
alex_h: ran an experiment forcing tiled GEMM on all GPUs: trace attached s3://perf-traces/run-1765123578-force-tiled.nsys. Results: tail latency improved ~28% but overall token/s dropped 6%.
cheng_li: tradeoff expected. we need a smarter selector: add warmup cost into kernel score so small microbatches don't pick high-setup kernels.
ravi_k: also saw H2D memcpy bursts in the timeline right before all-reduce. Could be KV fetches staging from host due to cache misses.
maria_g: do we have a perfetto view with the nvtx markers from runtime? that helps correlate kernel selection events to NVTX ranges.
alex_h: yes exported perfetto proto: s3://perf-traces/run-1765123456-perfetto.pb. NVTX shows markers: COMP:choose_kernel, COMP:launch, KV:prefetch_start, NCCL:allreduce_start.
perf-bot: note: INF-2418 linked to perf patch branch: fix/kernel-selector-warmup
cheng_li: proposal: implement kernel scoring tweak: score = latency_est + alpha * setup_cost + beta * variance_penalty. then run A/B with alpha=0.8.
ravi_k: also add a batching tweak: if microbatch_size < 0.6 * batch_max, pad to batch_max or push to next batch boundary. cheap to try.
maria_g: one more observation — when we force local KV routing, NCCL contention drops but memory pressure on single devices increases; watch OOMs on 80B configs.
alex_h: next steps I'll run three targeted captures: (A) baseline, (B) tiled-only kernel, (C) kernel-score+padding. will include --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl,osrt and perfetto export. adding owners: alex_h -> run captures, cheng_li -> implement scoring prototype, maria_g -> coordinate perfetto exports and dashboard comparisons.
cheng_li: ETA 2d for prototype. I’ll open a short PR with perf flags toggles.
alex_h: FYI tagged INF-2418 in the batch heuristics ticket. will post links here when uploads finish. thanks :thumbsup:
maria_g: great. if anyone wants to inspect the current perfetto quickly use https://perfetto.dev/ and load the pb from S3, search for "NCCL:allreduce_start" to see overlap patterns.
ravi_k: thanks — keeping an eye on the CI perf job for this run.
perf-bot: upload complete: s3://perf-traces/run-1765123720-summary.json (contains aggregated kernel durations and NCCL waits)
alex_h: OK closing loop here — I'll post a summary after the 3 captures.
